leadIn: After completing this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Apply the :is() pseudo-class to group multiple selectors for concise styling
Implement the :where() pseudo-class to create zero-specificity selector groups
Construct CSS rules using :is() to target nested elements efficiently
Configure selector lists with :where() to maintain low specificity in complex stylesheets
Manipulate element styling by combining :is() with other pseudo-classes
Integrate :where() into existing CSS to override styles without specificity conflicts
Update legacy CSS selectors by replacing comma-separated lists with :is() for better readability
